'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No data}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Zell Miller]]{{efn|In July 2000, Miller was appointed by Governor [[Roy Barnes]] to fill the vacancy caused by the death of Senator [[Paul Coverdell]].}} | before_party = Democratic Party (US) | after_election = [[Zell Miller]] | after_party = Democratic Party (US) }} {{ElectionsGA}} The '''2000 United States Senate special election in Georgia''' was held on November 7, 2000 to complete the unexpired term of the late [[Paul Coverdell]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Zell Miller]] won over [[Mack Mattingly]] in a landslide. Miller defeated Republican [[Mack Mattingly]], a former U.S. senator, in a landslide of over 20 points, carrying 149 of the state's 159 counties. Although this race was held on a [[Nonpartisanship|nonpartisan]] basis, the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] would not win a U.S. Senate seat in Georgia again until 2021, when [[Raphael Warnock]] won a [[2020–21 United States Senate special election in Georgia|special election]] to fill the same seat and [[Jon Ossoff]] won the [[2020–21 United States Senate election in Georgia|regular election]] for the Class 2 seat. Until 2026, this is the last time a Democrat won a Senate race in the state by double digits. == Background == Republican incumbent [[Paul Coverdell]] died suddenly of a [[Intracerebral hemorrhage|cerebral hemorrhage]] on July 17, 2000. Democratic governor [[Roy Barnes]] appointed former governor [[Zell Miller]] to fill the vacant seat until a successor could be duly elected. A special election to fill the remainder of Coverdell's term was scheduled for November 7, concurrent with [[2000 United States elections|regularly scheduled elections]]. ==Candidates== Under Georgia election law at the time, the special election would be non-partisan. Each candidate ran without a party label; the parties listed below are those with which the candidate would have run if given the opportunity: * Ben Ballenger (Republican) * Jeff Gates (Green) * Paul Robert MacGregor (Libertarian) * [[Mack Mattingly]], former ambassador to [[Seychelles]] and former U.S. senator (Republican) * [[Zell Miller]], incumbent U.S. senator and former governor (Democratic) * Winnie Walsh (Independent) * Bobby Wood (Republican) == Campaign == One of the biggest campaign issues was [[Social Security (United States)|Social Security]]; Miller attacked Mattingly for supporting a raise in the eligible age.{{Cite web|url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=MT&s_site=macon&p_multi=MT&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB76C8DCA04101C&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|title=Content no longer available|website=nl.newsbank.com}} Mattingly fought back by connecting Miller to Massachusetts senator [[Ted Kennedy]] and for a vote to block legislation aimed at protecting Social Security. Mattingly sought to gain support by tying the campaign to the presidential election at the top of the ticket. He said he would vote for the Republican nominee, [[Texas Governor|Texas governor]] [[George W. Bush]], who was very popular in the state, and challenged Miller to publicly state which presidential candidate he supported. Miller conceded he would vote for his party's nominee, vice president [[Al Gore]], because as governor, Miller had worked with Gore on [[Emergency management|drought relief]], [[welfare reform]], and the [[Atlanta Olympics]]. "That does not mean I agree with all of his policies," Miller concluded.{{Cite web|url=https://www.augustachronicle.com/|title=The Augusta Chronicle: Local & World News, Sports & Entertainment in Augusta, GA|website=The Augusta Chronicle}} In early October, a poll showed Miller leading with 59% of the vote, despite the fact that Bush was leading Gore by a double-digit margin.{{Cite web|url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=CL&s_site=ledgerenquirer&p_multi=CL&p_theme=realcities&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB722D10F9BD7F7&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|title=Content no longer available|website=nl.newsbank.com}} ===Debates=== *[https://www.c-span.org/video/?159785-1/georgia-senatorial-debate Complete video of debate], October 15, 2000 === Polling === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign="bottom" ! scope="col" |Poll source ! scope="col" |Date(s) ! scope="col" style="width:75px;" |Sample
